component.name: Kinetics
component.summary: How a substance moves through you

description.p: Kinetics plots what happens to a substance after you take it: how much reaches the blood, how fast, where it goes in the body, what it turns into, and how long it really takes to leave. Move the cursor across the curve and it explains the phase you are in.

It covers twenty substances — everyday ones like caffeine, alcohol and paracetamol, and commonly used or misused ones including opioids, stimulants, sedatives, dissociatives and psychedelics. Each was chosen to demonstrate a different principle of pharmacokinetics: saturable elimination, flip-flop kinetics, redistribution into tissue, prodrug activation, genetic variation in metabolism, and the lag between a blood level and an effect.

Several substances can be placed on one timeline at once, which is where the real risk usually lives. When a combination is known to be dangerous — an opioid with a sedative, alcohol with almost anything — the overlap is drawn and the mechanism explained.

Every parameter comes from published literature and carries its citation. This is a teaching and harm-reduction tool, not a clinical or dosing calculator: it shows the shape of what happens, not what will happen to any particular person.
